items.title: Local failure with globally smooth convex branches
items.note: local_failure states the theorem existentially, in the TeX's order: four functions f_i (convex, ContDiff ℝ 2, Hessian globally Lipschitz in the Euclidean operator norm: C^{2,1}) with 0 ⪯ ∇²f_i ⪯ 64I (RadialHessian.matrix, the matrix of fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f_i); since f_i is C², it is differentiable everywhere with a differentiable derivative map, so this is the classical Hessian of failure.tex:485-487, A/failure/prose/059); for F = max_i f_i (variable with its defining equation): compact sublevels, F(0) ≤ F, F(x) = F(0) → x = 0, F not differentiable at 0; then starts x ℓ 0 → 0 with H ℓ 0 = I and the run data (iterates, matrices, gradients, lengths, trial lists, limits x̄_ℓ) chosen before (c₁,c₂), so the objective, starts, initial matrix and complete decision tree (the trial lists with the accepted length, which determine every bracketing decision) are the same for all pairs; for every 0<c₁≤1/3, c₁<c₂<1 and ℓ ≥ 1 an AdmissibleBFGSRun with these data (infinite, full BFGS, actual gradients) whose lengths are the outputs of the specified search NonStrictLineSearch.fromMetric with constants (c₁,c₂) and any trial budget N ≥ 5 ('produces'; such a run is unique: implemented_run_unique); x_k → x̄_ℓ ≠ 0, F(x_k) strictly decreasing to F(x̄_ℓ) > F(0) = 0, 0 ∉ ∂F(x̄_ℓ); every queried point x_k + a(-H_kg_k), a in the trial list, is differentiable; at most five trials; accepted lengths 1, 1/4, 1/16 repeating; the set of Euclidean norms of all queries of the ℓth run is bounded and its supremum tends to 0. The runs are indexed by ℓ ≥ 1 as in the proof (failure.tex:388). Witnesses: the library's D construction (DEmbedding.branch, DEmbedding.objective, DEmbedding.center, DEmbedding.run); the proof (failure.tex:387-427) is covered in A_failure (proof/003, disp/025-028).
